newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-HOUGHTON BELIEVES ZIMBABWE HAVE TURNED THE CORNER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HOUGHTON BELIEVES ZIMBABWE HAVE TURNED THE CORNER.

text.p: Recent successes in the one-day arena prove Zimbabwe have turned the corner in international cricket, according to the man in the best position to judge.
Dave Houghton, player-coach with the ninth and latest test-playing nation, made history when he captained Zimbabwe against India in his country's inaugural test five years ago.
In an otherwise unmemorable match, Houghton scored a century and, although his best days are behind him, remained an essential member of the side against England and India this season.
Houghton is quietly satisfied after a season during which Zimbabwe beat England 3-0 and India 1-0 in one-day series and held out for a draw in both tests against England.
Zimbabwe wrapped up their first one-day series victory against India after Monday's second and final match between the two sides was called off at Harare Sports Club because of a waterlogged ground.

"This completes an incredibly good season for us," Houghton said in an interview. "We've basically gone the whole year unbeaten at home and that's always a good start. We spoke at the beginning of our season about what we could do to improve our cricket and we agreed that our focus had to be on being pretty good at home.
"Only then can you start talking about whether you can win away. So I'm delighted with our performances from that aspect."
Houghton, who also coaches English county Worcestershire, is quick to concede that India's cricketers were fatigued after their long tour of South Africa.

"They were pretty tired and looked very jaded after their long tour there. But still, Bulawayo was a one-day international and you've got to play well to win, our guys were up for it and the Indians weren't."

Zimbabwe, given test status in 1992, had to wait nine years for their second one-day victory after an upset win over Australia in the 1983 World Cup. Their one-day record now, while hardly earth-shattering, is a little more respectable -- played 72, won 12, tied three, lost 55, two no results.
In their last 10 one-day games, Zimbabwe have won five, tied once and lost four and Houghton believes this improvement in one-day consistency stems from a more positive mental approach to the game.

"For me, as a coach, 90 percent of my job this season has been mental. I've worked very hard on the motivational side, putting motivational placards up in the change-room, giving Winston Churchill-type speeches, and things like that, and it's worked

"What's happened, the turnaround over the last two or three months, is that we've now got a team of guys who believe that they're going to win every time they walk on the park. It doesn't matter who they're playing against.
"They're not silly enough to think they're world champions and that they'll never lose, because obviously we do lose. But the whole atmosphere in the changing room is now completely different."
Zimbabwe's record in the test arena is unimpressive, their only victory in 22 tests remaining a home win over Pakistan.

"I think we've been beaten eight times and we've drawn the rest and that's obviously not a huge record,'' Houghton concluded. '''But, if we can turn the corner in test cricket as we have at one-day level, I think that'll be the breakthrough that Zimbabwe cricket needs.''
